name: Tasks
description: A queue of prompts Claude does one after another, each in its own chat or continuing the one before. Every task reports back how it went: outcome, summary, things to know and follow-ups, in one table with links to the chats. Each project has its own queue, and every run is kept in its history. Claude can queue tasks too, after you review and edit them.

tools.description: Reports how the task-queue task this chat is running went. Call it once when the task is done or can't go on (only in a chat that runs a queued task; the instructions say so). The user reads the reports as a table instead of reading the chat. It also takes late reports: an earlier task of this chat that ended without a report (No report, or interrupted) is reported with its taskId, which the instructions and the queue's request name; report those first. Only this chat's own tasks. Never change the task queue with jig_set_addon_data: this tool is the only way to report.

outcome.description: done, partial (some of it), failed, or blocked (needs something from the user)

summary.description: What you did and the result, in two or three sentences

notes.description: Things the user should know: decisions you took, risks, anything surprising (short lines)

followUps.description: Follow-up tasks you suggest, each a prompt that could be queued on its own

taskId.description: The task to report when it isn't the one running now: an earlier task of this chat without a report (its id, e.g. t3). Leave out for the running task

tools.description: Adds tasks to the user's task queue, which Claude works through one after another, each reporting back. Use it when the user asks to queue work, e.g. one task per spec, document, issue or item of a list. Each prompt must stand alone (it usually runs in a new chat): say what to do and where the material is (file paths). It returns the queue.

tasks.description: The tasks in order: each a prompt string, or { title, prompt, newChat } (newChat false continues the previous task's chat)

project.description: The project's name; leave out for this chat's project

sameChat.description: All tasks continue one chat instead of each starting a new one (default false)

start.description: Start the queue right away; only when the user said so

tools.description: Changes tasks that are still queued (not running or finished): their title, their prompt, text appended to the prompt, whether they are left out of the run, whether they continue the previous task's chat (newChat), and where they are in the queue (moveTo). Moves follow the Queue tab's rules: never above or between tasks that ran; a task that lands inside a chat continues it, between chats it starts its own unless newChat is false; wholeChat moves the task's whole chat, only between chats. Edits apply in order and all or nothing: a broken rule changes nothing and says why. Safe while the queue runs: it changes only those tasks, never the queue's status. Always use it instead of jig_set_addon_data for the queue. addon_tasks_list gives the ids.

tasks.description: One entry per task: { id, title?, prompt? (replaces it), append? (added on a new paragraph at the end), leftOut?, newChat? (false continues the chat of the task before it, true starts a new one; the first task in the queue can't continue), moveTo? ("top", "bottom", { after: id } or { before: id }), wholeChat? (with moveTo: move every task of its chat) }

project.description: The project's name; leave out for this chat's project

tools.description: The user's task queue: each task's status and report summary.
